title: The Elements — a children's guide to the periodic table
description: All 118 chemical elements with kid-friendly descriptions, atomic numbers, charge (oxidation) states, fun facts, and their most common compounds. Includes Chinese names for every element and its top 5 compounds.

chineseNote.whyRadicalsMatter: Chinese element names are wonderfully logical: the radical (the piece on the left or bottom of the character) tells you what kind of element it is. 气 means it is a gas, 钅means it is a metal, 石 means it is a solid nonmetal, and 氵or 水 means it is a liquid. There are only two liquid elements, and both carry the water radical: 溴 (bromine) and 汞 (mercury).

radicalLegend.气: gas — e.g. 氢 hydrogen, 氧 oxygen, 氦 helium
radicalLegend.钅: metal — e.g. 铁 iron, 铜 copper, 金 gold
radicalLegend.石: solid nonmetal — e.g. 碳 carbon, 硫 sulfur, 硅 silicon
radicalLegend.氵/水: liquid — only 溴 bromine and 汞 mercury

chineseNote.rareGlyphWarning: The 14 elements marked nameZhRareGlyph use very new, rare characters (elements 104-118). They need a font with CJK Extension B/F coverage or they render as tofu boxes. Provide a webfont fallback or show the pinyin instead.

elements.name: Hydrogen

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Hydrogen is the smallest and lightest atom in the whole universe: just one proton with one electron whizzing around it. It is also the most common element anywhere — about three quarters of all the stuff in space is hydrogen. Stars like our Sun are giant balls of hydrogen squeezing together to make light and heat.
funFacts: If the periodic table were a race, hydrogen would win for being first AND lightest.
The Sun burns about 600 million tons of hydrogen every single second.
Two hydrogen atoms plus one oxygen atom make water — so you are mostly made of hydrogen by atom count.
Hydrogen gas is so light that a balloon filled with it floats up and away.
Rockets use liquid hydrogen as fuel because it packs a huge punch for its weight.

compounds.name: Water
compounds.about: The most important compound on Earth — you drink it, swim in it, and are made of it.

compounds.name: Methane
compounds.about: Natural gas that cooks food on a stove; also what cows burp.

compounds.name: Ammonia
compounds.about: A sharp-smelling gas turned into fertilizer that grows much of the world's food.

compounds.name: Hydrochloric acid
compounds.about: A strong acid — your own stomach makes it to digest lunch.

compounds.name: Hydrogen peroxide
compounds.about: Water with an extra oxygen; it fizzes on cuts and bleaches hair.

compounds.name: Sulfuric acid
compounds.about: The world's most-produced chemical, used inside car batteries.

compounds.name: Glucose
compounds.about: The sugar plants make from sunlight and your body burns for energy.

compounds.name: Ethanol
compounds.about: The alcohol in hand sanitizer and in some car fuels.

compounds.name: Sodium hydroxide
compounds.about: Also called lye — used to make soap and unclog drains.

compounds.name: Hydrogen sulfide
compounds.about: The rotten-egg gas that bubbles out of swamps and volcanoes.

elements.name: Helium

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Helium is the second lightest element and the ultimate loner — it almost never joins up with other atoms, so it has no real compounds. It was discovered on the Sun before anyone found it on Earth, by studying sunlight through a prism. Today we collect it from underground gas wells.
funFacts: Helium was found on the Sun first — it is the only element discovered in space before Earth.
Breathing a little helium makes your voice squeaky because sound travels faster through it.
Helium is the only substance that never freezes solid, no matter how cold it gets, unless you also squeeze it.
Below −271 °C liquid helium becomes a 'superfluid' that can climb up the walls of its container.
Party balloons use only a tiny slice of our helium; most cools the giant magnets in hospital MRI scanners.
elements.compoundsNote: Helium is a noble gas and forms no stable everyday compounds. Chemists have only made fragile molecules like HeH+ (helium hydride) inside special equipment — it was also the very first molecule ever to form in the universe.

compoundsExamples.name: Helium hydride ion
compoundsExamples.about: Thought to be the first molecule ever made after the Big Bang; spotted in space in 2019.

elements.name: Lithium

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

elements.description: Lithium is the lightest metal of all — so light it floats on water, though it fizzes and reacts the moment it touches it. It is soft enough to cut with a butter knife. Lithium is the superstar of rechargeable batteries in phones, laptops and electric cars.
funFacts: Lithium is so light it would float on water — if it did not react with it first.
It must be stored under oil, because plain air makes it tarnish.
Lithium burns with a beautiful crimson-red flame, used in fireworks.
The battery in your phone shuttles lithium ions back and forth every time you charge it.
Lithium is one of only three elements made in the Big Bang itself, along with hydrogen and helium.

compounds.about: The material inside most phone and laptop batteries.

compounds.name: Lithium carbonate
compounds.about: The main lithium chemical mined from salt flats; also a medicine.

compounds.name: Lithium chloride
compounds.about: A salt so thirsty for water it is used to dry out air.

compounds.name: Lithium hydroxide

compounds.name: Lithium iron phosphate

compounds.name: Lithium fluoride

compounds.name: Lithium hydride

compounds.name: Lithium nitrate

compounds.name: Lithium aluminum hydride

elements.name: Beryllium

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

elements.description: Beryllium is a light, stiff, silvery metal that is stronger than steel for its weight. It hides inside famous gemstones — emeralds and aquamarines are both beryllium crystals colored by tiny impurities. Beryllium dust is poisonous, so only trained scientists handle it.
funFacts: Emeralds and aquamarines are the same beryllium mineral, just different colors.
The mirrors on the James Webb Space Telescope are made of beryllium because it barely shrinks in the cold of space.
Beryllium is transparent to X-rays, so it makes the windows on X-ray machines.
Mixed with copper it makes tools that cannot spark — vital near explosive fuels.
It is one of the lightest metals, yet a beryllium beam is stiffer than a steel one.

compounds.name: Beryl
compounds.about: The gemstone mineral that gives us emerald and aquamarine.

compounds.name: Beryllium oxide
compounds.about: A ceramic that carries heat like a metal but does not conduct electricity.

compounds.name: Beryllium hydroxide
compounds.about: The white powder made when beryllium ore is first processed.

compounds.name: Beryllium fluoride
compounds.about: A glassy solid used in some experimental nuclear reactor fuels.

compounds.name: Beryllium chloride
compounds.about: Forms long chain-like structures, unusual for a simple salt.

compounds.name: Phenakite
compounds.about: A rare, very hard gemstone mineral.

compounds.name: Chrysoberyl
compounds.about: The gem alexandrite, which looks green in daylight and red in lamplight.

compounds.name: Beryllium sulfate
compounds.about: A water-soluble salt used in laboratories.

compounds.name: Beryllium carbonate
compounds.about: An unstable salt that easily gives off carbon dioxide.

compounds.name: Beryllium nitrate
compounds.about: Used to stiffen the glowing mantles in old gas lanterns.

elements.name: Boron
elements.nameMeaning: From borax, the mineral it was first found in

zhRadical.note: The 石 (stone) radical — this element is a solid nonmetal.

elements.description: Boron sits on the fence between metals and non-metals, so it is called a metalloid. Pure boron is a hard, dark, brittle solid, almost as hard as diamond. You meet boron every day in heat-proof glass, laundry powder and the slime you can make at home.
funFacts: Boron makes glass that will not crack when it goes from the oven to the counter — that is Pyrex.
Borax plus glue is the classic recipe for homemade slime.
Boron carbide is so hard it is used in bulletproof vests and tank armor.
Boron gobbles up neutrons, so it is used in nuclear reactor control rods to slow reactions down.
Plants need a tiny amount of boron to grow — too little and their leaves curl up.

compounds.name: Borax
compounds.about: A soft white mineral used in laundry detergent and slime recipes.

compounds.name: Boric acid
compounds.about: A mild antiseptic, and a very effective ant and cockroach powder.

compounds.name: Boron trioxide
compounds.about: The ingredient that makes heat-proof borosilicate glass.

compounds.name: Boron carbide
compounds.about: One of the hardest materials known — used for armor plating.

compounds.name: Boron nitride
compounds.about: Comes in a slippery form like pencil lead and a hard form like diamond.

compounds.name: Boron trifluoride
compounds.about: A gas that chemists use to kick-start reactions.

compounds.name: Sodium borohydride
compounds.about: A handy chemical for adding hydrogen to other molecules.

compounds.name: Diborane
compounds.about: A strange molecule where hydrogen atoms act like bridges.

compounds.name: Calcium hexaboride

compounds.name: Boron trichloride

elements.name: Carbon

zhRadical.note: The 石 (stone) radical — this element is a solid nonmetal.

elements.description: Carbon is the element of life. Every living thing on Earth — you, your dog, trees, mushrooms — is built on carbon because carbon atoms link into long chains and rings like Lego bricks. The same element can be soft gray pencil lead or the hardest diamond, depending only on how the atoms are arranged.
funFacts: Diamond and pencil lead are both pure carbon — only the atom arrangement differs.
About 18% of your body's weight is carbon.
Carbon atoms can bond into hollow soccer balls called buckyballs and tubes called nanotubes.
Graphene, a sheet of carbon one atom thick, is the strongest material ever measured.
Carbon dating uses a rare radioactive carbon to work out how old ancient bones and wood are.

compounds.name: Carbon dioxide
compounds.about: The gas you breathe out and plants breathe in; also the fizz in soda.

compounds.name: Methane
compounds.about: Natural gas — the simplest carbon compound and a powerful greenhouse gas.

compounds.name: Glucose
compounds.about: The sugar that fuels every cell in your body.

compounds.name: Calcium carbonate
compounds.about: Chalk, limestone, seashells and eggshells are all made of it.

compounds.name: Carbon monoxide
compounds.about: An invisible, odorless and dangerous gas from incomplete burning.

compounds.name: Ethanol
compounds.about: The alcohol in sanitizer, made by yeast eating sugar.

compounds.name: Acetic acid
compounds.about: What makes vinegar sour.

compounds.name: Caffeine
compounds.about: The wake-up molecule in coffee, tea and cocoa.

compounds.name: Cellulose
compounds.about: The tough fiber that builds plant walls, wood and paper.

compounds.name: Sodium bicarbonate
compounds.about: Baking soda — it makes cakes rise and volcanoes erupt.

elements.name: Nitrogen

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Nitrogen makes up 78% of the air you are breathing right now — every breath is mostly nitrogen. As a gas it is very lazy and refuses to react, which is handy: it keeps chips fresh in their bags. But locked into compounds, nitrogen becomes the key ingredient of fertilizer, proteins and DNA.
funFacts: Four out of every five molecules in the air are nitrogen.
Liquid nitrogen is −196 °C and can freeze a flower solid enough to shatter.
Chip bags are puffed up with nitrogen to stop the chips going stale and getting crushed.
Your DNA and every protein in your body contains nitrogen atoms.
Lightning splits nitrogen in the air, letting plants use it — a natural fertilizer factory.

compounds.name: Ammonia

compounds.name: Nitric acid

compounds.name: Ammonium nitrate

compounds.name: Nitrous oxide

compounds.name: Nitrogen dioxide

compounds.name: Potassium nitrate

compounds.name: Urea

compounds.name: Hydrogen cyanide
compounds.about: Extremely poisonous, but also found in space clouds where life's chemicals form.

compounds.name: Nitric oxide
compounds.about: A messenger molecule your blood vessels use to relax and widen.

compounds.name: Nitroglycerin

elements.name: Oxygen

discovered.by: Joseph Priestley and Carl Wilhelm Scheele

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Oxygen is the element you cannot live without — you use it every few seconds to burn food for energy. It is the most common element in the Earth's crust and in your body. Almost half of every rock under your feet is oxygen locked into minerals.
funFacts: About 65% of your body weight is oxygen, mostly because you are mostly water.
Nearly half of the Earth's crust, by weight, is oxygen.
Fire cannot burn without oxygen — that is why a lid smothers a flame.
The oxygen you breathe was made by plants, algae and tiny ocean bacteria.
Liquid oxygen is pale blue and is attracted to magnets.

compounds.name: Water
compounds.about: Covers 71% of the planet and fills most of your body.

compounds.name: Silicon dioxide
compounds.about: Sand, quartz and glass — the most common mineral in the crust.

compounds.name: Carbon dioxide
compounds.about: Breathed out by animals, drunk in by plants.

compounds.name: Iron oxide
compounds.about: Rust, and the red color of Mars.

compounds.name: Aluminum oxide
compounds.about: The mineral corundum; ruby and sapphire are colored versions.

compounds.name: Calcium carbonate
compounds.about: Limestone, chalk and seashells.

compounds.name: Ozone
compounds.about: Three oxygen atoms; high in the sky it blocks the Sun's harmful rays.

compounds.name: Hydrogen peroxide
compounds.about: A fizzing bleach and disinfectant.

compounds.name: Calcium oxide
compounds.about: Quicklime — a key ingredient in cement.

compounds.name: Sulfuric acid
compounds.about: The most-manufactured chemical in the world.

elements.name: Fluorine

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Fluorine is the greediest element of all — it grabs electrons from almost anything and reacts with nearly every other element. As a pure pale-yellow gas it is fiercely dangerous, yet once it is safely bonded it protects your teeth in toothpaste and stops eggs sticking to your frying pan.
funFacts: Fluorine is the most reactive element in the entire periodic table.
Chemists tried for 70 years to isolate it; several were poisoned trying.
Non-stick pans are coated in Teflon, a plastic wrapped in fluorine atoms.
Fluoride in toothpaste rebuilds tooth enamel and fights cavities.
The mineral fluorite glows in the dark under UV light — the word 'fluorescent' comes from it.

compounds.name: Fluorite
compounds.about: The main fluorine mineral; it glows under ultraviolet light.

compounds.name: Sodium fluoride
compounds.about: Added to toothpaste and some tap water to protect teeth.

compounds.name: Teflon (PTFE)
compounds.about: The slippery non-stick coating on frying pans.

compounds.name: Hydrofluoric acid
compounds.about: So aggressive it dissolves glass; used to etch patterns on it.

compounds.name: Sulfur hexafluoride
compounds.about: A heavy gas that makes your voice go deep — the opposite of helium.

compounds.name: Uranium hexafluoride
compounds.about: Used to separate types of uranium for nuclear fuel.

compounds.name: Cryolite
compounds.about: Helps melt aluminum ore so the metal can be extracted.

compounds.name: Stannous fluoride
compounds.about: Another tooth-protecting fluoride found in toothpaste.

compounds.name: Chlorofluorocarbons
compounds.about: Old fridge gases, now banned for damaging the ozone layer.

compounds.name: Fluorine gas
compounds.about: The pure element — pale yellow and the most reactive gas known.

elements.name: Neon

zhRadical.note: The 气 (gas) radical — this element is a gas.

elements.description: Neon is a noble gas that refuses to react with anything at all, so it has no compounds. Its claim to fame is light: run electricity through neon and it glows a brilliant orange-red. That glow lit up the signs of cities all over the world for a hundred years.
funFacts: Neon signs only glow orange-red; other colors come from different gases or coatings.
Neon was named 'new' by a 12-year-old — the discoverer's son suggested it.
Neon is the fifth most common element in the universe but very rare on Earth.
A neon light has no filament to burn out, so signs can last for decades.
Liquid neon is a far better refrigerant than liquid helium for its volume.
elements.compoundsNote: Neon is the least reactive element known. It forms no chemical compounds at all — not even fragile laboratory ones. Scientists have only ever coaxed it into loose 'clusters' held together by weak attraction, such as Ne–Ne pairs in ultra-cold experiments.

elements.name: Sodium
elements.nameMeaning: From English soda; symbol Na from Latin natrium

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

elements.description: Sodium is a soft silver metal you can slice like cheese — but drop a piece in water and it fizzes, dances and can burst into flame. Amazingly, when sodium joins with the poisonous gas chlorine, the result is completely safe: ordinary table salt.
funFacts: A dangerous metal plus a poisonous gas makes harmless table salt.
Sodium is soft enough to cut with a plastic knife.
It burns with a bright yellow-orange flame — the color of old street lamps.
Your nerves fire signals by pumping sodium in and out of cells, so you need salt to think.
Sodium must be kept under oil, or it reacts with the moisture in air.

compounds.name: Sodium chloride
compounds.about: Table salt — in the sea, in your food and in your blood.

compounds.name: Sodium bicarbonate
compounds.about: Baking soda, for rising cakes and fizzing science experiments.

compounds.name: Sodium hydroxide
compounds.about: Lye — used to make soap and clear blocked drains.

compounds.name: Sodium carbonate
compounds.about: Washing soda, and a key ingredient in making glass.

compounds.name: Sodium nitrate
compounds.about: A mined fertilizer once called Chile saltpetre.

compounds.name: Sodium sulfate
compounds.about: Used in powdered laundry detergent.

compounds.name: Sodium fluoride
compounds.about: The cavity fighter in toothpaste.

compounds.name: Sodium silicate
compounds.about: 'Water glass' — a glue and the base for growing crystal gardens.

compounds.name: Sodium hypochlorite
compounds.about: Household bleach, which also disinfects swimming pools.

compounds.name: Sodium benzoate
compounds.about: A preservative that keeps sodas from going moldy.

elements.name: Magnesium
elements.nameMeaning: From Magnesia, a district in Greece

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

elements.description: Magnesium is a light, strong metal that burns with a blinding white light — so bright that old cameras used it for flash photography. It is also at the very heart of every green plant: the molecule that captures sunlight has a magnesium atom in its middle.
funFacts: Every leaf is green because of chlorophyll, and every chlorophyll molecule holds one magnesium atom.
Burning magnesium is so bright it can hurt your eyes, and water makes the fire worse.
It is one third lighter than aluminum, so racing cars and laptops use magnesium parts.
Epsom salts for aching muscles are a magnesium compound.
Your body needs magnesium for over 300 different jobs, including making bones.

compounds.name: Magnesium oxide
compounds.about: A heat-proof lining for furnaces; also an antacid.

compounds.name: Epsom salt
compounds.about: Added to baths to soothe sore muscles.

compounds.name: Magnesium carbonate
compounds.about: The white chalk gymnasts and climbers use to dry their hands.

compounds.name: Magnesium hydroxide
compounds.about: Milk of magnesia, which settles an upset stomach.

compounds.name: Magnesium chloride
compounds.about: Spread on icy roads and used to make tofu firm.

compounds.name: Chlorophyll
compounds.about: The green pigment that lets plants turn sunlight into food.

compounds.name: Dolomite
compounds.about: A rock so common that a whole Italian mountain range is named after it.

compounds.name: Olivine
compounds.about: A green mineral that makes up much of the Earth's mantle.

compounds.name: Talc

compounds.name: Magnesium diboride

elements.name: Aluminum
elements.nameMeaning: From alum, a compound used since ancient times

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

elements.description: Aluminum is the most common metal in the Earth's crust, and it is light, shiny and does not rust. Yet 200 years ago it was so hard to extract that it cost more than gold — emperors served dinner on aluminum plates to show off. Today it is your soda can and aluminum foil.
funFacts: Aluminum was once more valuable than gold; the top of the Washington Monument is a small aluminum cap.
Recycling a can uses only about 5% of the energy needed to make a new one.
It does not really rust — a thin invisible oxide layer instantly seals the surface.
Ruby and sapphire are both aluminum oxide with a pinch of coloring impurity.
Airplanes are largely aluminum because it is strong but light enough to fly.

compounds.name: Aluminum oxide
compounds.about: Corundum — used as sandpaper grit, and as ruby and sapphire gems.

compounds.name: Aluminum hydroxide
compounds.about: An antacid, and a flame retardant in carpets.

compounds.name: Aluminum chloride
compounds.about: A workhorse chemical for building new molecules.

compounds.name: Alum
compounds.about: Used for thousands of years to fix dye into cloth.

compounds.name: Kyanite

compounds.name: Cryolite

compounds.name: Bauxite

compounds.name: Kaolinite

compounds.name: Aluminum nitride

elements.name: Silicon

zhRadical.note: The 石 (stone) radical — this element is a solid nonmetal.

elements.description: Silicon is the second most common element in the ground, and almost every rock, grain of sand and pane of glass contains it. Purified into perfect crystals, it becomes the brain of every computer, phone and games console — which is why the world's tech capital is called Silicon Valley.
funFacts: Every computer chip starts life as sand.
Silicon is a semiconductor: sometimes it conducts electricity, sometimes it does not — perfect for switches.
Chip-making silicon is 99.9999999% pure, one of the purest materials humans make.
Glass, sand, quartz and opal are all silicon-and-oxygen compounds.
Silicon is not the same as silicone — silicone is the bendy rubbery stuff made from it.

compounds.name: Silicon dioxide
compounds.about: Sand, quartz, and the main ingredient of glass.

compounds.name: Silicon carbide
compounds.about: Nearly as hard as diamond; used for grinding and in fast electronics.

compounds.name: Silicon nitride
compounds.about: A tough ceramic used in ball bearings and engine parts.

compounds.name: Silicic acid
compounds.about: Dissolved silicon in water; diatoms use it to build glass shells.

compounds.name: Sodium silicate
compounds.about: Water glass — a glue, sealant and crystal-garden starter.

compounds.name: Feldspar
compounds.about: The single most abundant mineral group in the Earth's crust.

compounds.name: Olivine
compounds.about: The green gemstone peridot; makes up much of Earth's mantle.

compounds.name: Kaolinite
compounds.about: Fine white clay for pottery and porcelain.

compounds.name: Silane

compounds.name: Silicones

elements.name: Phosphorus

zhRadical.note: The 石 (stone) radical — this element is a solid nonmetal.

elements.description: Phosphorus was discovered by a man boiling down buckets of urine hoping to make gold — instead he got a waxy solid that glowed in the dark. Phosphorus is essential to life: it forms the backbone of your DNA and makes your bones and teeth hard.
funFacts: It was the first element discovered by a known person, from 5,500 liters of urine.
White phosphorus glows green in the dark and catches fire in air by itself.
The rungs and rails of your DNA ladder are held together by phosphorus.
The strip on a matchbox contains red phosphorus — the safe kind.
Your body's energy currency, ATP, is a phosphorus molecule used billions of times a day.

compounds.about: The mineral that makes your bones and teeth hard.

compounds.name: Phosphoric acid

compounds.name: Adenosine triphosphate

compounds.name: Phosphorus pentoxide

compounds.name: Hydroxyapatite

compounds.name: Ammonium phosphate
compounds.about: One of the world's most-used fertilizers.

compounds.name: Phosphorus trichloride

compounds.name: Sodium tripolyphosphate
compounds.about: Once added to detergents to soften water.

compounds.name: Phosphorus sesquisulfide
compounds.about: The chemical in strike-anywhere match heads.

elements.name: Sulfur

zhRadical.note: The 石 (stone) radical — this element is a solid nonmetal.

elements.description: Sulfur is the bright yellow element that collects in crusty crystals around volcanoes. On its own it barely smells, but its compounds are behind some of the world's worst pongs: rotten eggs, skunk spray and stink bombs. Ancient people called it brimstone.
funFacts: Sulfur is one of the few elements found pure in nature, in yellow lumps near volcanoes.
The rotten-egg smell is not sulfur itself but hydrogen sulfide gas.
Skunk spray, onion tears and garlic breath are all sulfur compounds.
Adding sulfur to rubber, called vulcanizing, is what makes car tires tough.
Sulfuric acid is the most produced chemical on Earth by weight.

compounds.name: Sulfuric acid
compounds.about: Used in car batteries, fertilizer and almost all industry.

compounds.name: Hydrogen sulfide

compounds.name: Sulfur dioxide
